We evaluate the models here against a large number of simulated chronologies and
radiocarbon samples. To save ourselves some time, we also run these simulations
in parallel. Generally speaking, running torch models in parallel is a bad idea
since torch has built-in parallelism that could lead to thread contests. We try
to account for this by limiting the number of threads in each parallel process
to one. Running my PC at full tilt on 14 of 16 cores reduces the total wall time
(in hours) for the evaluation by an order of magnitude.

Each simulation looks like the example above, following the generative model.
The steps are as follows:

1. Sample a starting year.
2. Simulate a chronology.
3. Sample dates from the chronology.
4. Calibrate the dates.
5. Train models with dates.
6. Infer chronology and sample ages.
7. Evaluate models.

These steps are repeated for each simulation. Currently, there are 3 (n_years)
\* 3 (n_samples) \* 3 (n_clusters) \* 3 (distribution) = 81 starting conditions
that are repeated 28 times each, resulting in 2268 unique simulations with
randomization.

**Metrics**

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{MAE} &= \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} \hspace{2pt} \mathbb{E} \left| [\hat{t}_{i} \mid F_{i}] - t_{i} \right| \\
\text{TVD} &= 0.5 \sum_{j=1}^{m} \hspace{2pt} \left| v_{j} - \hat{v}_{j} \right|
\end{aligned}
$$

```{r}
#| label: metrics
#| file: R/metrics.R
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: R/metrics.R
#| eval: false
```

**Simulations**

```{r}
#| label: model-evaluation
#| cache: true
#| time_it: true
#| output: false
# define starting conditions for simulations
evaluation_grid <- expand.grid(
  n_years = c(500, 2500, 12500),
  n_samples = c(50, 250, 1250),
  n_clusters = c(1, 3, 9),
  distribution = c("gaussian", "uniform", "skewed"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# repeat each combination n times
i <- rep(seq_len(nrow(evaluation_grid)), times = 28)
evaluation_grid <- evaluation_grid[i, ]
rownames(evaluation_grid) <- NULL

n_iter <- nrow(evaluation_grid)

# set up clusters
clusters <- makeCluster(14)

fns <- c(
  "bgmm.R",
  "calibrate.R",
  "ckde.R",
  "constants.R",
  "dataframe-helpers.R",
  "dpmm.R",
  "metrics.R",
  "mixture-helpers.R",
  "netc14.R",
  "sample-dates.R",
  "simulate-chronology.R",
  "spd.R"
)

clusterExport(
  clusters,
  varlist = c("fns", "evaluation_grid", "intcal20"),
  envir = environment()
)

clusterEvalQ(clusters, {
  library(carbondate)
  library(torch)
  torch_set_num_threads(1)
  lapply(file.path("R", fns), source)
})

# run simulations in parallel
evaluation_results <- parLapply(clusters, seq_len(n_iter), \(i) {
  set.seed(STARTREK + i)

  # scenario
  n_years <- evaluation_grid[["n_years"]][i]
  n_clusters <- evaluation_grid[["n_clusters"]][i]
  n_samples <- evaluation_grid[["n_samples"]][i]
  distribution <- evaluation_grid[["distribution"]][i]
  start <- sample(seq(100, 49500 - n_years), 1)
  end <- start + n_years - 1

  # simulate chronology, draw samples, and calibrate
  chronology <- simulate_chronology(start, end, n_clusters, distribution)
  samples <- sample_dates(chronology, n_samples, intcal20)
  calibrated_dates <- calibrate(samples, intcal20)

  # training
  models <- list(
    ckde(calibrated_dates),
    bgmm(calibrated_dates),
    dpmm(samples),
    netc(calibrated_dates),
    spd(calibrated_dates)
  )

  # evaluation
  years <- seq(start, end)
  true_ages <- samples[["cal_age"]]

  evaluations <- lapply(models, \(.model) {
    .density <- density(.model, years)[["density"]]
    .ages <- predict(.model, calibrated_dates)

    data.frame(
      tvd = tvd(.density, chronology),
      wd = wd(.density, chronology),
      mae = mae(.ages, true_ages),
      mse = mse(.ages, true_ages)
    )
  })

  evaluations <- do.call(rbind, evaluations)

  # baseline
  oracle_ages <- predict(chronology, calibrated_dates)
  mae_oracle <- mae(oracle_ages, true_ages)
  mse_oracle <- mse(oracle_ages, true_ages)

  # collect and return
  e_clusters <- vapply(models, count_components, integer(1))
  elapsed <- sapply(models, attr, which = "elapsed")

  sim <- data.frame(
    iter = i,
    model = c("CKDE", "BGMM", "DPMM", "NetC14", "SPD"),
    start = start,
    n_years = n_years,
    n_samples = n_samples,
    n_clusters = n_clusters,
    distribution = distribution,
    e_clusters = e_clusters,
    mae_oracle = mae_oracle,
    mse_oracle = mse_oracle,
    elapsed = elapsed
  )

  cbind(sim, evaluations)
})

# close parallel processes and collect results
stopCluster(clusters)
evaluation_results <- do.call(rbind, evaluation_results)
```

Save results.

```{r}
#| label: save-evaluation
write.csv(
  evaluation_results,
  "data/evaluation-results.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```
